analytical_models.equation_role: γ_SFE = 2ρΔG^(γ→ε) + 2σ (Eq. 3), where ρ is the molar surface density along {111} planes, ΔG^(γ→ε) is the molar Gibbs energy of the γ→ε transformation and σ is the γ/ε interfacial energy per unit area
analytical_models.model_note: Calculated room-temperature γ_SFE of the 6Al austenite (6Al_γ) = 62.64 mJ·m^-2 (Table 2).

parameters.name: σ (γ/ε interfacial energy per unit area)

interfaces.interface_notes: In the 6Al steel the minority ferrite (α) grains reside mostly at the austenite grain boundaries, forming a γ/α duplex structure. The general duplex steel stress-partitioning/interface behavior reported in the paper (high stress at α/γ interfaces activating edge dislocations) is demonstrated specifically on the 8Al steel, not the 6Al steel.
interfaces.phase_evolution: With increasing Al content the phase constitution of the Fe-35Mn-xAl-0.1C steels evolves from single-phase austenite (4Al) to austenite-matrix duplex (6Al) and then to ferrite-matrix duplex (8Al, 10Al); the 6Al steel is the austenite-matrix duplex member of this sequence.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: As-cast ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-6Al-1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W (wt%) prepared via vacuum induction melting under a high-purity Ar atmosphere.
As-cast ingots homogenized at 1150 °C for 4 h.
Homogenized ingots subsequently hot-forged into rods with a diameter of 16.5 mm.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: hot-forged into rods with a diameter of 16.5 mm

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Bars solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by oil quenching to achieve a microstructure with nearly equiaxed grains; this terminal treatment defines the 6Al sample and is shared by all four designed steels.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: at least three tensile specimens tested to fracture for reproducibility; interrupted tensile tests to engineering strains of 3 %, 10 %, 20 % and 28 %
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: standard cylindrical tensile specimens 5 mm in diameter, 25 mm in gauge length, machined from quenched rods with tensile axis parallel to the rod axis

tensile_properties.strain_hardening_rate: 6Al shows typical three-stage strain hardening labeled A, D and E (Fig. 3d)
tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: engineering stress-strain and true stress-strain curves for 6Al shown in Fig. 3(a, c); 6Al exhibits typical three-stage strain-hardening behaviour (stages A, D and E)

structures.overall_structure: Solution-treated 6Al steel is an austenite-based duplex lightweight steel with quasi-equiaxed grains; the austenite matrix (γ) contains numerous annealing twin boundaries and L1_2-type short-range ordered domains, while sparse minority ferrite (α) grains reside mostly at grain boundaries and contain coexisting B2 and DO3 ordered domains.

defects.type: dislocation cell blocks / dense dislocation bands

phases_present.morphology: elongated aligned dark banded contrast (dense dislocation bands); dislocation cell blocks (same as other Al contents)
straight parallel planar slip bands (less pronounced planar slip than 8Al ferrite)

structures.overall_structure: After tensile deformation the 6Al steel shows distinctly different deformation mechanisms in austenite and ferrite: the austenite deforms by dislocation cell blocks/dense dislocation bands, while the ferrite exhibits pronounced planar slip forming straight slip bands.

unmapped_findings: Measured composition of the 6Al steel (Table 1): Mn 35.14, Al 5.97, C 0.095, Nb 0.11, V 0.10, Mo 1.24, W 0.95 wt% (Fe balance).

Phase compositions of the 6Al steel (Table 1): austenite 6Al_γ — Mn 35.92, Al 5.88, C 0.098, Nb 0.09, V 0.09, Mo 1.12, W 0.86 wt% (Fe balance); ferrite 6Al_α — Mn 32.44, Al 6.83, C not detected ('-'), Nb 0.09, V 0.18, Mo 1.54, W 1.63 wt% (Fe balance); Al partitions into ferrite.
The room-temperature stacking-fault energy (γ_SFE) of the 6Al austenite (6Al_γ) is 62.64 mJ·m^-2, calculated by the thermodynamic approach (Eq. 3) using parameters from literature [35] (Table 2).
Density of the 6Al steel measured by the Archimedes principle is 7.18 g cm^-3.

The austenite of the 6Al steel contains L1_2-type short-range ordered (SRO) domains, evidenced by satellite spots (011_SRO reflection) near the γ reflections in the [100]γ SADP; these are attributed to concentration fluctuations of Al and C atoms, indicating spinodal decomposition occurred during quenching.

In the 6Al steel, DO3 ordered domains coexist within both the B2 ordered domains and the ferrite matrix; the maximum DO3 ordered domain size in 6Al ferrite is estimated to be approximately 2.0 nm (smaller than 8Al ~2.1 nm and 10Al ~19 nm).
Unlike the 8Al steel, which exhibits five distinct strain-hardening stages (A, B, C, D and E), the 6Al steel exhibits typical three-stage strain-hardening characteristics labeled A, D and E.

The microhardness of ferrite is significantly higher than that of austenite in the designed steels, indicating ferrite acts as a strengthening phase; the 6Al ferrite microhardness (first point of the α series at 6 wt% Al) lies between the 240 and 270 HV gridlines of Fig. 2(b), while the austenite microhardness rises only modestly from ~150 HV (4Al) to just under 210 HV (10Al).

The paper reports that the excellent strength-ductility balance (attributed to edge-dislocation activity plus dynamic slip band refinement, DSBR) is a feature of the 8Al ferrite-based duplex steel; the 6Al steel is the austenite-matrix duplex member of the designed Fe-35Mn-xAl-0.1C series and shows less pronounced ferrite planar slip than the 8Al steel.
